summary: This work systematically investigates measurement-induced state transitions (MIST) in transmon qubits as a function of offset charge $n_g$ and demonstrates that engineered fast-load and fast-clear pulse shaping suppresses MIST without complex waveforms or feedback. A three-step pulse scheme minimizes both readout and post-readout error probabilities across the full $n_g$ range by controlling diabaticity at avoided crossings via Landau-Zener dynamics.
motivation: MIST fundamentally limits readout speed and fidelity in dispersive readout of superconducting qubits, and is particularly sensitive to charge noise in transmons due to charge dispersion of higher-lying levels, making $n_g$-dependent mitigation strategies necessary for robust operation.
method: Two charge-sensitive transmons ($E_J/E_C \approx 34-40$) with active gate-voltage control were used to map $P_m$ versus $n_g$ and photon number under different pulse profiles. Floquet branch analysis predicted resonant avoided crossings; consecutive readout pulses (M2 and M3) isolated ring-up versus combined ring-up/ring-down contributions using $\tau_\mathrm{up} = \tau_\mathrm{down} = 100$ ns with $\tau_\mathrm{up} + \tau_\mathrm{ss} = 4$ µs.
result: For readout (M2), the calibrated two-step pulse reduced $n_g$-averaged total error $P_\mathrm{err}^i$ relative to square pulses across $70 < n_\mathrm{ss} < 1000$ by suppressing resonator photon overshoots and achieving fast ring-up. For post-readout (M3), the three-step pulse achieved lowest $P_\tilde{\mathrm{err}}^i$ for $|0\rangle$ state by enforcing symmetric diabatic passage through avoided crossings, demonstrating QND preservation without hardware overhead.
